references.text: The law's provision that lepers must live outside the camp, which also applies to Miriam's seven-day isolation.
A reminder of what the Lord did to Miriam when they left Egypt, referring directly to this event.
The seven-day period for cleansing from leprosy, corresponding to Miriam's seven days of isolation.
An example of being cast out or excluded, as Miriam was shut out from the camp.
Spitting in the face as a sign of disgrace and shame, illustrating the meaning of the expression that her father had spit in her face.
Spitting in the face as public disgrace, parallel to the shame described in the Lord's words to Moses.
Spitting as an expression of contempt and disgrace, highlighting the seriousness of God's words that her father had spit in her face.
